messages:
Maya: Quick sync — pulled together RFC feedback and sketched three "anchors" for compatibility: gateway, runtime, and sidecar. link: https://redwood.internal/notes/anchoring-draft
Aj: Nice. Can you summarize the biggest tradeoffs?
Maya: Sure — gateway anchor: normalizes once at edge, keeps runtime simple, lower overall CPU, but problematic for streaming and partial responses. runtime anchor: apply compatibility layer in the serving runtime, great for streaming and per-model behavior, but increases per-request CPU and operational surface. sidecar: best of both for private deployments, localizes translations per-pod but adds orchestration complexity.
Liam: Streaming is the blocker for gateway. If the gateway buffers to rewrite frames we add latency or memory pressure.
Sophie: For private deployments sidecar seems attractive — tenants can opt-in without touching the central runtime.
Maya: Telemetry implications: gateway anchor collapses a lot of signals unless we pass through client_version headers and per-request metadata. We need to preserve X-Client-Surface.
Aj: Agree — propose header name: X-Client-Surface: v2. Also add X-Compat-Shadow to mark shadowed requests.
Maya: Rollout proposal: 1) tenant-level opt-in flag; 2) gateway shadow decode (no rewrite) for 7d; 3) 10% traffic rewrite; 4) 100% for qualified tenants.
Aj: Add metrics to watch: decode_latency_p50/p90, streaming_frame_drop_rate, schema_mismatch_rate.
Sophie: Also watch cache hit-rate. Gateway normalization can reduce embed-prefix cache effectiveness if it touches ordering or whitespace semantics.
Maya: We'll define a tight canonicalizer that only strips/rewrites explicitly listed fields. No heuristic rewriting.
Liam: Example canonicalizer (sketch):
```
def canonicalize(body):
  # strip ephemeral fields
  body.pop('client_trace', None)
  # normalize messages array to minimal fields the runtime cares about
  body['messages'] = [ { 'role': m.get('role'), 'content': m.get('content') } for m in body.get('messages', []) if m.get('role') ]
  return body
```
Maya: Good. Acceptance criteria for anchor choice: p50 latency delta <= 2%, p90 delta <= 5%, streaming integrity no frame mutation, and function-calls preserved.
Aj: How do we map old model ids to variants? A mapping table in config-store plus a fallback policy?
Maya: Yes — store has mapping + quality guardrails. Policy: prefer exact match, if not available use mapped variant with gradual fallback.
Sophie: Per-request escape hatch? Add X-Compat-Bypass: true header for admin clients so they can opt-out per call. Rate-limit usage.
Liam: If we allow per-request bypass, restrict to admin tokens. Otherwise we're opening traffic to inconsistent behaviors.
Maya: Security note: ensure any header-based toggles are validated against token scopes.
deploy-bot: deploy started: compat-gateway-shadow v1 -> staging :rocket:
Aj: Action items: Aj to prototype gateway shadowing tool (ETA 1 week), Liam to set up streaming fuzz harness (ETA 2w), Sophie to draft telemetry dashboards and alerts, Maya to update RFC with anchor decision and rollout ops.
Maya: One more: for sidecar deployments, pinning policy should prefer sidecar translation for latency-sensitive tenants and runtime anchor only for hosted tenants.
Sophie: I'll add that to the rollout doc and the console UX mock (tenant opt-in toggle).
Maya: Thanks everyone — will update RFC and ping for another quick sync after the prototype. :thumbsup:
